### When is Black Friday?

Black Friday is on Friday 27 November 2026. 

Some retailers limit their deals to Black Friday weekend (which runs from 27 November until Cyber Monday, on 30 November). But these days, many start offering their discounts from the beginning of the month - which is why some people refer to the sales period as ‘Black November’.

## When is Black Friday 2026?

Black Friday historically falls on the Friday immediately after Thanksgiving in the United States. In 2026, Black Friday will take place on Friday 27 November, with Cyber Monday – traditionally the online-only day of the sale, which now concludes Black Friday – following on Monday 30 November.

There are always huge savings on beauty to be had 

Nessa Humayun/The Standard

Although Black Friday once lasted for just one day, many retailers now launch their promotions weeks in advance. This extended shopping period, often called Black November, allows consumers to compare prices and spread out their purchases rather than rushing to find bargains on a single day.

In the UK, major retailers such as Amazon, Currys, John Lewis and Argos regularly participate in the event. Their offers can cover a wide range of products, including televisions, smartphones, laptops, kitchen appliances, clothing and beauty products. The discounts continue through the weekend and into Cyber Monday – often getting bigger and better.

Gloria and Pickles | John Lewis & Partners | Christmas Ad 2026

- Black Friday 2026 is just around the corner, offering shoppers the chance to secure discounted items ahead of the Christmas period. 
- This year, the annual shopping event will take place on 27 November, while Cyber Monday is set to follow on 30 November. 
- Experts have listed key dos and don’ts to help shoppers navigate their spending sprees, including looking for additional discounts by going through cashback websites and checking for extra voucher codes. 
- Black Friday customers are also advised to read return policies, as well as to make a wish list and budget.
- Greg Zakowicz, an expert at e-commerce marketing platform Omnisend, says: “A good retailer should have a clear and fair return policy, especially during sales events. If it’s difficult to find or overly restrictive, think twice before purchasing.”
